# HeatmapR

**HeatmapR** draws complex, publication-ready heatmaps in R. It handles
everything from a quick look at a table to clustered heatmaps of
hundreds of thousands of cells. Dendrograms, annotations and legends are
laid out for you, and there are dot plots and other plots for
single-cell data. It is fast enough for single-cell data, needs nothing
beyond R to install, and comes with an app to build heatmaps in the
browser. Visit the [website](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/)
to get started.

## Why HeatmapR?

- **Much faster, with a fraction of the memory.** Clustering and drawing
  a heatmap of 20,000 rows takes **0.6 seconds and 114 MB**. pheatmap,
  `heatmap.2()`,
  [`stats::heatmap()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/heatmap.html) and
  ComplexHeatmap take 32 seconds to 2 minutes and 3.3 to 4.7 GB.
  HeatmapR clusters large data in two stages by default; clustering
  exactly, as the others do, it takes 7.1 seconds and 1.5 GB. A 3,000 ×
  3,000 matrix takes 4 seconds instead of over 4 minutes. 100,000 rows
  take 1.2 seconds, where every other package ran out of memory.
- **Built for single-cell data.**
  [`heat_map()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map.md)
  takes `SingleCellExperiment`, `Seurat`, `flowSet` and AnnData data as
  they are, as well as sparse and on-disk matrices. Features are chosen
  by name, and cells are grouped and annotated by their metadata. There
  are also dot plots, markers, gene-set scores, compositions, contrasts
  and trajectories. A heatmap of 40 genes in 100,000 cells takes 1.3
  seconds, against 40 seconds and 2.8 GB with Seurat’s `DoHeatmap()`.
- **Complete figures from one call.** Dendrograms, cluster splits,
  annotation tracks, bar plots, labels and legends are sized in inches
  from their contents. They’re laid out so that nothing overlaps,
  whatever the shape of the data or the size of the image, and
  [`heat_map_save()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_save.md)
  writes the figure at print resolution.
- **Point, click and keep the code.**
  [`heat_map_app()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_app.md)
  builds heatmaps in the browser and writes the R code that draws them
  again.
  [`heat_map_html()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_html.md)
  turns any heatmap into a web page to explore: hover for values, select
  rows and columns, search and zoom.
- **Ready for publication and analysis.**
  - [`heat_map_describe()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_describe.md)
    writes alternative text for screen readers.
  - [`heat_map_check_colours()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_check_colours.md)
    finds colours that colour-blind readers can’t tell apart.
  - [`heat_map_info()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_info.md)
    returns the order and clusters of the rows and columns for the rest
    of your analysis.
- **Nothing else to install.** HeatmapR uses base graphics and compiled
  C++, with no dependencies beyond R. pheatmap installs 13 other
  packages, ComplexHeatmap 18 and Seurat 129. HeatmapR is MIT licensed.

### HeatmapR and the alternatives

Time to draw a heatmap, in seconds, and the peak memory for 20,000 rows:

|  | HeatmapR | pheatmap | ComplexHeatmap | `heatmap.2()` | [`stats::heatmap()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/heatmap.html) |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Clustered, 20,000 × 30 | **0.6** (exact: 7.1) | 32 | 130 | 48 | 45 |
| Peak memory, 20,000 × 30 | **114 MB** (exact: 1.5 GB) | 4.7 GB | 3.7 GB | 4.7 GB | 3.3 GB |
| Clustered, 3,000 × 3,000 | **3.7** | 254 | 275 | 253 | 249 |
| Clustered, 100,000 × 30 | **1.2** | out of memory | out of memory | out of memory | out of memory |
| Not clustered, 3,000 × 3,000 | **0.6** | 8.8 | 26 | 250 | 4.5 |
| Other packages installed | **0** | 13 | 18 | 3 | 0 |

For single-cell data, against Seurat and scran:

|  | HeatmapR | Seurat or scran |
|:---|---:|---:|
| Heatmap of 40 genes in 100,000 cells | **1.3 s** | 40 s, 2.8 GB (`DoHeatmap()`) |
| Dot plot of 40 genes in 100,000 cells | **0.17 s** | 1.9 s (`DotPlot()`) |
| Markers of 12 groups, 20,000 cells and 20,000 genes | **0.4 s** | 19 s (scran’s `scoreMarkers()`) |

All times were measured on two cores with 7.8 GB of memory. For small
heatmaps, every package takes about a tenth of a second, except
ComplexHeatmap at about two seconds. The methods, and every size
measured, are in the [speed
comparison](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/articles/benchmarks.html)
and the [single-cell
guide](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/articles/single-cell.html#speed).
The numbers of packages are for the versions compared there.

## Features

Beyond clustering, scaling and customisable colours, shapes, sizes,
text, legends and layouts, **HeatmapR** can:

- **Show more than one value in each cell:**
  - split cells to compare two conditions (`cell_split`);
  - show the distribution of the values behind each cell
    (`cell_values`);
  - use cell size as a second variable;
  - fade colours towards grey where values are uncertain
    (`cell_uncertainty`).
- **Annotate rows and columns:**
  - metadata tracks (`annotation_x`, `annotation_y`);
  - bar graphs, box plots and violins beside the heatmap;
  - labels for chosen rows of a large heatmap (`mark_y`);
  - a zoom lens that enlarges a band of rows beside the whole
    (`zoom_y`).
- **Cluster with confidence:**
  - correlation and cosine distances;
  - optimal leaf ordering;
  - clustering within your own groups;
  - k-means splits;
  - bootstrap support drawn on the dendrogram branches
    (`tree_support_y`).
- **Handle large data:**
  - raster images for heatmaps with millions of cells;
  - two-stage clustering for a million rows;
  - [`heat_map_summarise()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_summarise.md)
    for pseudobulk heatmaps and dot plots of groups of cells;
  - robust, stepped or centred colour scales, with the distribution of
    the values traced over the legend.
- **Work with ggplot2:**
  - [`heat_map_grob()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_grob.md)
    places heatmaps beside `ggplot2` plots in `patchwork` and `cowplot`
    layouts;
  - [`heat_map_data()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_data.md)
    returns the cells, rows, columns and dendrograms as tidy data, for
    rebuilding or restyling them.

## Build heatmaps in the browser

[`heat_map_app()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_app.md)
opens an app to build a heatmap without writing code. You can drop a
table or a single-cell file on it, or start it from data in R. Then:

- choose a heatmap, a dot plot or a correlation heatmap;
- set any argument of
  [`heat_map()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map.md)
  while the heatmap redraws, with values on hover and selections on the
  heatmap;
- download the figure, with the R code that draws it again.

It needs the shiny and bslib packages. [Building heatmaps in the
browser](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/articles/app.html)
shows how it works.

``` r

heat_map_app()                                         # drop a file, or choose an example
heat_map_app(mtcars, scale = "column", tree = "both")  # start from data in R
```

![The HeatmapR app with a clustered heatmap of mtcars: the sections of
the settings on the left with plain labels and argument names, the
changed settings above the heatmap, and the values of a cell on
hover.](reference/figures/README-app.png)

[`heat_map_html()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_html.md)
writes any heatmap as a single web page that works without R. Hover for
values; click or drag over cells, labels and dendrograms to select rows
and columns; then copy or download the selection, search and zoom.

## Single-cell data

**HeatmapR** reads single-cell data where it lives -
`SingleCellExperiment` and `Seurat` objects, `flowFrame` and `flowSet`
objects, AnnData (`.h5ad`) files and sparse matrices, in memory or on
disk (DelayedArray, HDF5Array and BPCells) - choosing features by name
and grouping and annotating cells from their metadata. Only the chosen
features of the cells shown are made dense, so a few markers of a
million cells need little memory, and summaries, markers and scores of
every gene read on-disk data a block of genes at a time.

- **Dot plots, markers and gene-set scores** -
  [`heat_map_dot()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_dot.md)
  draws the mean of each group as colour and the proportion of its cells
  detected as size (or two conditions in the halves of each dot),
  [`heat_map_markers()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_markers.md)
  ranks the markers of each group by their AUC, with Wilcoxon p-values,
  ready to pass to `features` or to draw as a dot plot, and
  [`heat_map_score()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_score.md)
  scores each cell for sets of genes (z-scored means or module scores).
- **Compositions and contrasts** -
  [`heat_map_composition()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_composition.md)
  draws the share of each cell type in each sample, and
  [`heat_map_contrast()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_contrast.md)
  the log fold change between two conditions in each cluster, tested on
  pseudobulks with the samples as replicates.
- **Aligned heatmaps** -
  [`heat_map_align()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_align.md)
  lines up data sets measured on the same cells or groups, such as genes
  and surface proteins, as blocks of one heatmap, each scaled and
  coloured on its own with its own legend, with the rows clustered on
  one of them.
- **Summaries of groups** -
  [`heat_map_summarise()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_summarise.md)
  finds the mean, median, sum or proportion detected of each feature in
  each group of cells from sparse data in compiled code, and `group_max`
  keeps small groups visible next to large ones.
- **Cytometry** - the asinh transform and quantile scaling of markers,
  the medians of clusters in each sample, and stacked bars of the events
  of each condition in each cluster.
- **Trajectories** -
  [`heat_map_smooth()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_smooth.md)
  smooths genes along pseudotime, one lineage at a time, and
  `tree_order_y = "peak"` orders them by when they peak.

[`heat_map_example()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_example.md)
simulates blood cells, cytometry events and a branching trajectory to
try them on:

``` r

cells <- heat_map_example("rna")
markers <- heat_map_markers(cells, group_by = "cell_type", n = 3)
heat_map_dot(cells, features = markers, group_by = "cell_type")
```

[TABLE]

The
[guides](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/articles/index.html)
on the website cover ordering, large heatmaps, [single-cell
data](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/articles/single-cell.html),
cells, and working with other packages, and the
[changelog](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/news/index.html)
lists everything new in **HeatmapR** 2.0.0.

## Installation

**HeatmapR** can be installed from CRAN:

``` r

install.packages("HeatmapR")
```

The development version can be installed directly from GitHub:

``` r

devtools::install_github("DillonHammill/HeatmapR")
```

**HeatmapR** contains C++ code: CRAN provides ready-built binaries for
Windows and macOS, but installing from GitHub (or from source) needs a
compiler - [Rtools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/) on
Windows or the Xcode command line tools on macOS.

## Usage

Creating heatmaps is as easy as loading **HeatmapR** and supplying your
dataset to the
[`heat_map()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map.md)
function. For details on customising your heatmaps, refer to the package
vignette.

``` r

library(HeatmapR)
heat_map(
  mtcars,
  scale = "column",
  scale_method = "range",
  tree_x = TRUE,
  tree_y = TRUE,
  tree_cut_x = 4,
  tree_cut_y = 12,
  cell_size = TRUE,
  cell_shape = "circle",
  title = "mtcars"
)
```

![Heatmap of the mtcars data rescaled within each column, drawn as
circles sized and coloured by value, with dendrograms splitting the cars
into 12 groups and the variables into 4
groups.](reference/figures/README-HeatmapR-1.png)

## Acknowledgements

**HeatmapR** computes distances and hierarchical clustering in compiled
code that follows the methods of the `stats` package
([`stats::dist()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/dist.html) and
[`stats::hclust()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/hclust.html)), which it
still uses for the methods the compiled code doesn’t cover. Dendrograms
are drawn by **HeatmapR**’s own code. Versions up to 1.1.0 drew them
with modified functions of the
[ggdendro](https://github.com/andrie/ggdendro) package, which were
removed in 2.0.0.

Code of
Conduct](https://contributor-covenant.org/version/2/0/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.html).

follows:

citation("HeatmapR")

# Package index

## Draw heatmaps

- [`heat_map()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map.md)
  : Create a complex heatmap using base graphics
- [`heat_map_cor()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_cor.md)
  : Correlation heatmaps with ellipses, numbers and dendrograms
- [`heat_map_dot()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_dot.md)
  : Dot plots of the features of groups of cells
- [`heat_map_align()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_align.md)
  : Heatmaps of the same rows side by side, each with its own colour
  scale
- [`heat_map_composition()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_composition.md)
  : Heatmaps of the make-up of samples: the share of each group of cells
- [`heat_map_contrast()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_contrast.md)
  : Heatmaps of the differences between two conditions in each group of
  cells
- [`plot(`*`<heat_map>`*`)`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map-methods.md)
  [`print(`*`<heat_map>`*`)`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map-methods.md)
  : Draw a heat_map object
- [`heat_map_style()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_style.md)
  : Styles: settings of heat_map() set once and reused
- [`heat_map_app()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_app.md)
  : Build a heatmap in the browser

## Inspect and describe heatmaps

Extract the order, clusters, colours and layout of a heatmap, or
describe it in plain language as alternative text.

- [`heat_map_info()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_info.md)
  : Extract information about a constructed heatmap
- [`heat_map_describe()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_describe.md)
  : Describe a heatmap in plain language
- [`print(`*`<heat_map_description>`*`)`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/print.heat_map_description.md)
  : Print a heatmap description as wrapped text
- [`heat_map_check_colours()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_check_colours.md)
  : Check that the colours of a heatmap can be told apart with
  colour-vision deficiencies
- [`heat_map_html()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_html.md)
  : Interactive heatmaps: a web page to explore and select from

## Use heatmaps with other tools

Combine heatmaps with ggplot2 plots, or export their contents as tidy
data.

- [`heat_map_grob()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_grob.md)
  : Convert a heatmap into a grob for grid and ggplot2 layouts
- [`heat_map_data()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_data.md)
  : Extract the contents of a heatmap as tidy data

## Prepare data

Scale, summarise and cluster data before (or while) drawing a heatmap.

- [`heat_map_read_h5ad()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_read_h5ad.md)
  : Read an AnnData (.h5ad) file
- [`heat_map_scale()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_scale.md)
  : Scale numeric data prior to constructing heat_map
- [`heat_map_summarise()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_summarise.md)
  : Summarise groups of rows or columns for a heatmap
- [`heat_map_markers()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_markers.md)
  : Find the marker features of groups of cells
- [`heat_map_score()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_score.md)
  : Scores of gene sets in each cell
- [`heat_map_smooth()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_smooth.md)
  : Smooth features along pseudotime for a heatmap
- [`heat_map_downsample()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_downsample.md)
  : Downsample cells within groups
- [`heat_map_clust()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_clust.md)
  : Perform hierarchical clustering for heatmap
- [`heat_map_threads()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_threads.md)
  : Number of threads used by HeatmapR

## Example data

Simulated single-cell RNA, cytometry and trajectory data for trying the
functions.

- [`heat_map_example()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_example.md)
  : Simulated single-cell data for examples

## Arrange and save heatmaps

Arrange heatmaps with other plots in custom layouts and save high
resolution images.

- [`heat_map_arrange()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_arrange.md)
  : Arrange heatmaps side by side on shared colour and size scales
- [`heat_map_custom()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_custom.md)
  : Create a custom heatmap plot layout
- [`heat_map_layout()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_layout.md)
  : Arrange multiple heatmaps
- [`heat_map_new()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_new.md)
  : Open a popup graphics device for heatmaps
- [`heat_map_record()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_record.md)
  : Record a custom heatmap
- [`heat_map_complete()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_complete.md)
  : Indicate when a heatmap is complete and ready for saving
- [`heat_map_save()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_save.md)
  : Save high resolution images
- [`heat_map_reset()`](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/reference/heat_map_reset.md)
  : Reset all heatmap related settings

# Articles

### Get started

- [HeatmapR](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/articles/HeatmapR.md):

### Guides

Deeper looks at what HeatmapR can do, with every figure drawn as the
site is built.

- [Building heatmaps in the
  browser](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/articles/app.md):

  heat_map_app() builds heatmaps, dot plots and correlation heatmaps
  from a file or from data in R without writing code, and writes the R
  code that draws them again.

- [Ordering rows and
  columns](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/articles/ordering.md):

  Dendrogram, optimal leaf and spectral orders, how they work and when
  to use each, measured on clusters, a trajectory and a cycle.

- [Large
  heatmaps](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/articles/large-data.md):

  Hundreds of thousands of rows: raster drawing, two-stage clustering,
  k-means splits, automatic cuts, labels and zoom panels, threads and
  memory.

- [Single-cell
  data](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/articles/single-cell.md):

  Heatmaps, dot plots and markers straight from SingleCellExperiment,
  Seurat, flowFrame and sparse matrices: features by name, groups and
  annotations from metadata, downsampling, sparse summaries, marker
  ranking, cytometry and trajectories.

- [More than
  colour](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/articles/cells.md):

  Uncertainty, two values in a cell, distributions inside cells and
  beside the heatmap, metadata annotations, honest colour scales and
  correlations.

- [Working with
  heatmaps](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/articles/integration.md):

  Redrawing and saving heatmaps, extracting their orders and clusters,
  tidy data for ggplot2, heatmaps beside ggplot2 plots and alternative
  text for screen readers.

### Performance

- [Speed
  comparison](https://dillonhammill.github.io/HeatmapR/articles/benchmarks.md):

  The time and memory HeatmapR, ComplexHeatmap, pheatmap, gplots, stats
  and ggplot2 need to draw and cluster heatmaps from 10,000 to 9 million
  cells, and of clustering and leaf ordering on their own.
